exclusions.A: Tomas thought the burners had saved the orchard from being lost, and in June he said so again as he passed round the first bowl of apricots.
exclusions.B: Every one of them came from the corner tree.
exclusions.C: By morning every tree had come through, and the corner tree, forty yards from the nearest burner, had the best blossom on the place.
exclusions.E: The radio put the next frost in April, after the fruit had set, so the burners would be lit again only the next spring.

WV9-P03.5.note: The narrator sets Tomas's credit to the burners against the closing fact that every apricot came from the unburnered corner tree, a gentle, affectionate irony that reads as amused rather than reproachful, admiring, worried or nostalgic.
